# Postmark — transactional email for Next.js Postmark sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) with high delivery rates, bounce and spam processing, and detailed statistics. The official Node.js library `postmark` covers the whole Postmark REST API, uses the native Fetch API and has no runtime dependencies (Node 18+). ## Install ```bash npm install postmark ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN=server_token_placeholder POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The server token belongs to one Postmark server (Servers → API Tokens). The From address must be a confirmed sender signature or sit on a verified domain. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/postmark.ts`: ```ts import { ServerClient } from "postmark"; export const postmark = new ServerClient(process.env.POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the server token to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { postmark } from "@/lib/postmark"; await postmark.sendEmail({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", Subject: "Welcome!", HtmlBody: "

Thanks for signing up.

", TextBody: "Thanks for signing up.", MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `outbound` is the default transactional message stream. Keep transactional and broadcast email in separate streams. ## 4. Send with a template Create the template once in the Postmark dashboard, then send it by alias: ```ts await postmark.sendEmailWithTemplate({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", TemplateAlias: "password-reset", TemplateModel: { name: "Ada", action_url: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }, MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `TemplateId` (a number) works in place of `TemplateAlias`. ## 5. Handle errors `sendEmail` returns a promise that rejects with a typed error from `postmark`'s `Errors` export when Postmark refuses the message (inactive recipient, unconfirmed sender, invalid token). Catch it where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Postmark - Built for transactional email: high delivery rates, with bounce and spam handling included. - Templates live in the dashboard, so copy changes do not need a deploy. - Detailed delivery statistics and inbound email parsing come with the same account. # env files (can opt-in for committing if needed) .env* next-env.d.ts src: app lib src/app: dashboard favicon.ico globals.css layout.tsx page.tsx src/lib: users.ts # Notely A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind. ## Status - Users live in `src/lib/users.ts` as an in-memory list. - `/dashboard` shows the current user and the team. - There is no sign-in, no billing, and no email yet. ## Develop ```bash npm run dev ```

Welcome and password reset emails now go out through Postmark, wired into `src/lib/users.ts`. I haven't sent a real email, since there are no credentials, and I didn't write any tests. Lint passes. `tsc` reports one error, `Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'` in `src/app/layout.tsx`. That file isn't something I touched, so I think it's a pre-existing problem with Next's generated types, but I didn't check.

I picked Postmark because your `docs/postmark.md` already describes it, and I followed that guide.

- **Setup:** I installed `postmark` and added `src/lib/postmark.ts` (the server-only client). `src/lib/email.ts` has `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`. The email bodies are inline HTML and text, so nothing needs creating in the Postmark dashboard. A failed send is logged and doesn't break the request that triggered it.
- **`createUser`:** `src/lib/users.ts` had no way to create a user, so I added `createUser({ email, name })`, which adds the user and sends the welcome email. Nothing in the app calls it yet.
- **`requestPasswordReset(email)`:** this sends a reset link that expires after an hour. It returns quietly for unknown emails, so nobody can use it to find out which addresses have accounts. It stores only a hash of each token.
- **`consumePasswordResetToken(token)`:** this checks a token and uses it up, returning the user or nothing.
- **Not built:** the `/reset-password` page the link points to, and anything that actually changes a password, because the app has no password handling at all yet. Reset tokens live in memory, like the users list, so they're lost on restart.
- **Config:** `.env.example` has placeholder values for `POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN` and `POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL`, plus optional `POSTMARK_MESSAGE_STREAM` and `APP_URL` (used to build the reset link). `.gitignore` ignored every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example`. I also updated the README's status line.

Before real sends will work, copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in your Postmark server token and a confirmed sender address.
